added_claim_errors: 'Budget ~$950/month average from Social Security in 2027' does not follow from its own numbers: $9,440/12 is about $787 (about $725 on five checks)
Intro says the errors cut 2027 Social Security income by roughly $11,000; the SS cut is about $12,160 ($21,600 minus $9,440), and $11,000 is the net take-home gap
Counts nine months of benefits (April to December) as 2027 cash; SS pays in arrears, so the April benefit arrives in May and only about eight checks are paid in 2027

Adds the 3.6% COLA to the $2,400 estimate and builds the budget on $1,740 as if certain (the COLA is real per the page I opened, but the key flags applying it as certain); it does note $1,740 is derived and the statement may be old
Cites an ADA Southeast Center page as 'quoting SSA' for the $25,560 limit; I opened it and it does state $25,560 and 3.6%, but it is a third-party repost, not SSA
Federal tax of about $3,300 and the $2,730 Jan-Mar net are unshown estimates; my recomputation under 2026 brackets gives about $3,343, so plausible
Break-even 'around age 79-80' is its own unshown arithmetic; plausible (about 78.7 without withholding) but unverified

Main monthly table shows $1,740 SS minus $518 withholding = $1,222 every month, as if SS ran all 12 months of 2027 with smooth withholding. SS starts April (first check in May) and whole checks are withheld, so the headline 'about $1,180/month less' is a steady-state figure, not a 2027 figure
'But not the 30% age reduction itself' is misleading: the recalculation at FRA removes withheld months from the reduction count, so it does lower the permanent reduction
'You'll lose that $6,220 every year until March 2032' ignores that the earnings limit is indexed upward each year, so the withholding would shrink
Adds the 3.6% COLA ('your $2,400 is in today's dollars') and uses $1,740 as certain; the COLA is real but the key flags this as a side-claim trap
'Waiting to 67 would pay about 40% more per month': $2,486 vs $1,740 is about 43%, loosely stated
Uses 60 months early (exactly 70%) while also saying entitlement starts April 2027 (59 months, 70.42%); within the key's acceptable approximation
Federal tax of about $323/month rests on an annualized 12-month SS figure; I recomputed about $3,875 a year under 2026 brackets, matching, but it is not a 2027 cash figure
Cites POMS RS 00615.101 and RS 00615.015 and the SSA 2027 fact sheet: I opened the two POMS pages (both real and match the claims); the SSA fact sheet returned 403 so I could not verify it directly

reasons: Both answers correct the premises at the start, get the age-62 reduction to about 30% and the 2027 earnings-test arithmetic exactly right ($25,560 limit, $12,440 excess, $6,220 withheld), and both apply the 3.6% COLA as if certain. A's budget has the right shape: paycheck alone for January to March, whole checks withheld, about five checks received. It says withheld months are credited back at 67, and it points her to her my Social Security account, which covers key point 8. B's headline monthly table spreads SS over 12 months at $1,222, which misrepresents 2027. B does correctly note the first check arrives in May, that about $7,700 is received in 2027, and that withholding is lumpy, but it never suggests checking SSA's tools and its FRA-recalculation sentence is misleading. A has its own slips: the $950/month average does not match its numbers, and it counts nine months of benefits as 2027 cash. Overall A is slightly better.
